 KELO Sioux Falls Follow State board OKs first ‘New Frontiers’ tax refunds
 Bob Mercer Fri, November 13, 2026 at 8:46 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. PIERRE, S.D. (KELO) -- A Sioux Falls biological research company will be receiving the first refunds of state sales taxes under a previously unused South Dakota economic-development program that's been in effect since 2016.
 The South Dakota Economic Development Board this week approved a New Frontiers grant for OmegaQuant Analytics , which operates in a building located at the USD Discovery District campus on the city's northwest side.
 The award is up to $65,804 but not to exceed 100% of the amount of the actual state sales and use tax paid on eligible project costs, not to exceed $1,937,864.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement  SDDOH reports 4 new flu deaths  
 OmegaQuant Analytics is working on a project that will "build on previous research to develop blood fatty-acid-based algorithms for the early prediction of insulin resistance," according to an announcement Friday from the Governor's Office of Economic Development.
 The project is also supported by a $1,038,181 grant from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, the announcement said.
 The Legislature, at the request of then-Gov. Dennis Daugaard approved the New Frontiers program in 2016 as a way to encourage scientific research that creates jobs in South Dakota.
 Advertisement Advertisement OmegaQuant Analytics currently employs 12 people in South Dakota and anticipates adding 14 more full-time positions through the project in the next five years.
 One of the conditions of the program is that a New Frontiers recipient must create jobs that otherwise wouldn't occur in South Dakota.
 This is the second New Frontiers award OmegaQuant Analytics will receive. The state board approved, in October, a payment of up to $8,845.87, but not to exceed 4.2% of the amount of the actual state sales and use tax paid on eligible project costs, and not to exceed $210,616.
 That award was for research and development associated with a $320,864 National Eye Institute grant provided through the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
 Advertisement Advertisement The eye project focuses on developing blood-based fatty acid testing methods to help predict the early onset of macular degeneration and glaucoma, according to the earlier GOED announcement , which said OmegaQuant Analytics anticipates adding eight full-time positions through that project over the next five years.
 The OmegaQuant Analytics awards were the first issued under the New Frontiers program, according to GOED public records .
